contentBlocks.title: Social Relief of Distress (SRD R370) Grant
contentBlocks.description: Complete guide to the SASSA SRD R370 Grant (formerly R350): eligibility, how to apply online or via WhatsApp, payment dates, status checks, appeals, and everything beneficiaries need to know.

contentBlocks.targetGroup: Unemployed South Africans aged 18 to 59 with no income or financial support.

contentBlocks.text: The Social Relief of Distress (SRD) Grant, popularly known as the R370 grant (increased from R350 in 2025), is South Africa's largest social assistance programme by beneficiary numbers. It provides a monthly payment to unemployed adults who have no other source of income or government support. The grant has been extended to at least March 2027.

contentBlocks.text: Eligibility Criteria
To qualify for the SRD R370 grant, you must meet ALL of the following criteria:

items: South African citizen, permanent resident, refugee, asylum seeker, or special permit holder
Unemployed and not receiving any income
Not receiving any other social grant from SASSA
Not receiving UIF (Unemployment Insurance Fund) payments
Not receiving NSFAS (National Student Financial Aid Scheme) funding
No monthly bank deposits exceeding R624
Not living in a state-funded institution

contentBlocks.text: Grant Amount & Payment Schedule

The SRD grant is R370 per month. Payments are made between the 25th and the last day of each month. Unlike other SASSA grants, the SRD grant does not have a fixed single pay date — payments are rolled out progressively from the 25th onward. Some beneficiaries may receive payment earlier or later within this window depending on their bank or collection method.

rows: 25th to last day of each month
Bank EFT or Cash Send (retail collection)

contentBlocks.text: How to Apply for the SRD R370 Grant
The SRD grant application is fully online — you do not need to visit a SASSA office to apply. There are two ways to apply:
Method 1: Online Portal (srd.sassa.gov.za)

steps.title: Visit the SRD website
steps.description: Go to srd.sassa.gov.za on your phone, tablet, or computer.

steps.title: Enter your ID number
steps.description: Type in your 13-digit South African ID number. Asylum seekers and special permit holders should use their permit numbers.

steps.title: Enter your phone number
steps.description: Provide the mobile phone number registered in your name. SASSA will send an OTP to this number.

steps.title: Read and accept the declaration
steps.description: Read through the terms and conditions carefully. Tick the boxes to confirm you meet the eligibility criteria.

steps.title: Submit your application
steps.description: Click submit. You will receive a confirmation SMS with your application reference number.

contentBlocks.text: Method 2: WhatsApp

You can also apply via the SASSA WhatsApp line. Save 082 046 8553 to your phone contacts, send 'SASSA' to start the conversation, and follow the menu prompts to submit a new application. The WhatsApp service is free on most South African networks.
What Happens After You Apply

steps.title: Application received
steps.description: SASSA confirms receipt via SMS. Your application enters the verification process.

steps.title: Verification in progress
steps.description: SASSA checks your ID against Home Affairs, SARS, UIF, and NSFAS databases. Your bank account details are verified.

steps.title: Monthly evaluation
steps.description: After initial approval, your eligibility is reassessed every month through automated bank and database checks.

steps.title: Payment
steps.description: If approved for the month, payment is made between the 25th and 30th via bank EFT or Cash Send.

contentBlocks.text: Monthly Review Process — Important

contentBlocks.title: Your Status Changes Every Month
contentBlocks.text: Unlike other SASSA grants, the SRD grant is NOT permanently approved. Every month, SASSA re-evaluates your eligibility by checking your bank account and government databases. Your status can change from 'Approved' to 'Declined' from one month to the next based on your financial activity. Always check your status each month.
Documents Required

documents.label: Valid South African ID number (13 digits)
Mobile phone number registered in your name
Bank account details (for direct payment) or preference for Cash Send
Asylum seeker or special permit number (if applicable)

contentBlocks.text: How to Check Your SRD Status

You can check your SRD grant status through multiple channels. The most common method is the online portal at srd.sassa.gov.za — enter your ID number and the phone number used during application, verify with an OTP, and your status dashboard appears. You can also check via WhatsApp (082 046 8553), USSD (*134*7737#), or by visiting a SASSA office. For a complete guide, see our dedicated status check page.

contentBlocks.text: How to Appeal a Declined SRD Grant

If your SRD grant is declined for any month, you have the right to appeal. Appeals are handled by the Independent Tribunal for Social Assistance Appeals (ITSAA), not by SASSA itself. You have 90 days from the date of decline to submit your appeal. Because each month is evaluated separately, you must appeal each declined month individually.

steps.title: Visit the DSD Appeal website
steps.description: Go to srd.dsd.gov.za on your phone or computer.

steps.title: Enter your ID and phone number
steps.description: Provide your ID number and the phone number used in your application. Verify with the OTP sent to your phone.

steps.title: Select the month(s) to appeal
steps.description: Choose each month that shows 'Declined'. You can appeal multiple months in one session.

steps.title: Choose your reason for appeal
steps.description: Select the reason from the dropdown menu that matches your situation (e.g., 'Unemployed', 'No income', 'UIF mistake').

steps.title: Upload supporting documents
steps.description: Attach your sworn affidavit, bank statements, UIF termination letter, or NSFAS cancellation letter as evidence.

steps.title: Submit and save your reference number
steps.description: After submission, save your Appeal Reference Number. You will need it for follow-ups.

contentBlocks.text: Payment Methods

You can receive your SRD grant through two methods: direct bank transfer (EFT) to your personal bank account, or Cash Send (retail collection) at participating stores. You can switch between methods at any time through the SRD portal. Changes take effect from the following month.

contentBlocks.title: No Bank Account Needed
contentBlocks.text: You do not need a bank account to receive the SRD grant. Select 'Cash Send' as your payment method and collect your grant at any Pick n Pay, Shoprite, Boxer, Checkers, or Usave store using the SMS voucher sent to your phone.
Frequently Asked Questions

faqs.question: How long does the SRD grant last?
faqs.answer: The SRD grant has been extended to at least March 2027. It is reviewed annually by the government and may be extended further.

faqs.question: Why does my SRD status say 'Alternative Income Source'?
faqs.answer: This means SASSA found a bank deposit or registration in your name that suggests you have other income. Even a gift from family can trigger this. Appeal with a sworn affidavit explaining each deposit.

faqs.question: Can I get the SRD grant if I am working part-time?
faqs.answer: Only if your monthly earnings are below R624. If your bank account shows deposits exceeding R624 in any month, you will be declined for that month.

faqs.question: Do I need to reapply every month?
faqs.answer: No. Once your application is approved, SASSA automatically evaluates you each month. You do not need to reapply unless your grant was cancelled.

faqs.question: Can I get both SRD and another SASSA grant?
faqs.answer: No. You can only receive one social grant at a time. If you qualify for an Older Person, Disability, or Child Support Grant, you must choose one.

faqs.question: What if I turn 60 while receiving SRD?
faqs.answer: The SRD grant is for ages 18 to 59. Once you turn 60, you must apply for the Older Person Grant instead. Visit your nearest SASSA office to transition.

faqs.question: How do I change my payment method from bank to Cash Send?
faqs.answer: Log into the SRD portal at srd.sassa.gov.za, go to 'Payment Method', and switch from 'Bank Transfer' to 'Cash Send'. Changes apply from the next month.

faqs.question: Can I update my phone number for SRD?
faqs.answer: Yes. Log into the SRD portal and navigate to 'Update Personal Details'. You will need access to your old number for verification, or visit a SASSA office if you no longer have access.

faqs.question: What happens if my SRD status says 'Referred'?
faqs.answer: This means your application was flagged for fraud investigation. Contact the SASSA Fraud Hotline at 0800 60 10 11 and prepare to visit a SASSA office with your ID to resolve it.

faqs.question: Is the SRD grant taxable?
faqs.answer: No. SASSA social grants are exempt from income tax. You do not need to declare them on your tax return.
